chapters.title: Actuators
chapters.intro: All six joints use the same quasi-direct-drive actuator, a modified OpenQDD with a 9:1 helical planetary gearbox and a moteus driver on the back. Build the four hip actuators and the two wheel actuators the same way up to the last step; only the way they are closed differs.

steps.title: Heat-set inserts in the motor casing
steps.text: Start with the printed motor casing lying on its front face, back side up. The two inserts on the back hold the driver bracket later.

actions.cap: Place the motor casing on the bench, back side up.
Press the two M3 heat-set inserts into the back of the casing.

steps.title: Stator into the casing
steps.text: Turn the casing over. The stator drops into the casing from the front, then four M4 screws through the back of the casing clamp it.

actions.cap: Turn the casing over.
Lower the stator into the casing from the front, with its leads towards the cable slot.
Turn the casing over, holding the stator in place.
Fix the stator with four M4×10 socket-head screws from the back.

steps.title: Sun gear on the rotor
steps.text: Build the rotor next to the casing. The 8-tooth helical sun gear bolts to the front face of the rotor with four M3×18 screws.

actions.cap: Turn the casing over.
Set the rotor on the bench, magnets down, shaft up.
Fit the sun gear onto the rotor face, lining up the four holes.
Fasten the sun gear with four M3×18 socket-head screws.

steps.title: Rotor into the stator
steps.text: The rotor magnets pull hard on the stator. Hold the rotor by its rim, keep it centred and let it down slowly so the magnets do not slam onto the stator teeth.

actions.cap: Lower the rotor straight down over the stator until the shaft seats in the bearing.

steps.title: Encoder magnet
steps.text: Turn the motor over. The encoder magnet sits in a small holder on the end of the rotor shaft, facing the encoder chip on the driver board.

actions.cap: Turn the casing over.
Press the magnet holder onto the end of the rotor shaft.
Glue the encoder magnet into the holder.

steps.title: Driver board
steps.text: The driver bracket screws to the back of the casing. The board sits on the bracket with the encoder chip over the magnet, four self-tapping screws hold it, and the cover goes over the board and its screws.

actions.cap: Place the driver bracket over the magnet.
Fix the bracket with two M3×10 screws into the inserts.
Set the driver board on the bracket, encoder side down, connectors towards the cable slot.
Fix the board to the bracket with four 3×5 self-tapping screws.
Fit the driver cover over the board.

steps.title: Planet carrier
steps.text: The carrier is built beside the motor. Three planet gears turn on M3×14 screws between the two halves of the carrier; the top half is the output flange that the arm or the wheel bolts to.

actions.cap: Turn the casing over.
Set the bottom half of the planet carrier on the bench.
Press three M3 inserts into the bottom half.
Lay the cover disc in its recess.
Fix the disc with three M3×6 screws.
Place the three planet gears on their bosses.
Put the top half of the carrier on the planets.
Drive the three M3×14 screws through the top half and the planets; they are the planet axles, so stop when the planets still spin freely.
Press six M3 inserts into the output flange.

steps.title: Bearing housing
steps.text: The thin-section 75×95×10 bearing is a press fit in the printed housing. Push it in evenly all round; a flat plate over the bearing helps.

actions.cap: Set the bearing housing on the bench.
Press the 75×95×10 bearing into the housing.

steps.title: Gearbox half
steps.text: The carrier goes into the bearing from the front, then the ring gear slides over the planets. Turn the carrier slightly while lowering the ring so the helical teeth engage.

actions.cap: Lower the planet carrier into the bearing.
Slide the ring gear over the planets, turning the carrier until the teeth engage.

steps.title: Closing a wheel actuator
steps.text: The two wheel actuators close with eight M3×30 screws into inserts in the casing flange. Their output flange is the wheel hub. The four hip actuators stay open: they are closed through the hip plates in the next chapter.

actions.cap: Press eight M3 inserts into the front flange of the casing.
Lower the gearbox half onto the motor, turning it slightly so the sun gear slides between the planets.
Close the actuator with eight M3×30 socket-head screws.

chapters.title: Hip modules
chapters.intro: Each side of the body carries a hip module: one printed hip plate with the front and rear hip actuators. The two modules are mirror images.

steps.title: Front hip actuator on the X+ hip plate
steps.text: The hip plate is clamped between the gearbox half and the motor half of each actuator. Four M4×45 screws go in from the outside of the plate, through the ring gear and the bearing housing, into nuts held in the motor casing.

actions.cap: Stand the hip plate on the bench, outer face away from you.
Drop four M4 nuts into the hex pockets of the motor casing.
Seat the gearbox half in the front bore of the plate from the inside; the output flange shows on the outside.
Bring the motor half up behind it so the sun gear enters the planets.
Clamp the stack with four M4×45 socket-head screws from the outside of the plate.

steps.title: Rear hip actuator and cable gland
steps.text: The rear actuator goes into the second bore the same way. The cable gland in the plate carries the motor cables out of the body.

actions.cap: Drop four M4 nuts into the motor casing.
Seat the gearbox half in the rear bore.
Bring the motor half up behind it.
Clamp it with four M4×45 screws.
Push the M12 cable gland through the plate from the outside.
Tighten the lock nut on the inside.

steps.title: Front hip actuator on the X− hip plate
steps.text: The hip plate is clamped between the gearbox half and the motor half of each actuator. Four M4×45 screws go in from the outside of the plate, through the ring gear and the bearing housing, into nuts held in the motor casing.

actions.cap: Stand the hip plate on the bench, outer face away from you.
Drop four M4 nuts into the hex pockets of the motor casing.
Seat the gearbox half in the front bore of the plate from the inside; the output flange shows on the outside.
Bring the motor half up behind it so the sun gear enters the planets.
Clamp the stack with four M4×45 socket-head screws from the outside of the plate.

steps.title: Rear hip actuator and cable gland
steps.text: The rear actuator goes into the second bore the same way. The cable gland in the plate carries the motor cables out of the body.

actions.cap: Drop four M4 nuts into the motor casing.
Seat the gearbox half in the rear bore.
Bring the motor half up behind it.
Clamp it with four M4×45 screws.
Push the M12 cable gland through the plate from the outside.
Tighten the lock nut on the inside.

chapters.title: Frame and body
chapters.intro: The body is a frame of 20×20 aluminium profile. The hip modules bolt to its sides, the electronics sit inside on printed trays, and the belly with the retractable landing gear hangs underneath.

steps.title: Frame
steps.text: Cut the profiles to length and lay out the two side ladders, the front rails, the middle rail and the two long rear rails. The corner joints between profiles are not modelled in the CAD yet; join them with 2020 corner brackets or tapped ends, and keep the channel positions used by the T-nuts in the later steps free.

actions.cap: Lay out the X− side ladder: two 140 mm rails and two 53 mm posts.
Lay out the X+ side ladder.
Join the ladders with the two 228 mm front rails.
Add the 188 mm middle rail on top.
Add the two 400 mm rear rails.

steps.title: Hip modules on the frame
steps.text: Each hip module hangs on the outside of a side ladder from six M5×10 screws into drop-in T-nuts. Put the T-nuts in the outer channels first; drop-in nuts can also go in after the profiles are joined.

actions.cap: Drop six M5 T-nuts into the outer channels of the X+ ladder.
Hang the X+ hip module on the frame.
Fix it with six M5×10 socket-head screws.
Drop six T-nuts into the X− ladder.
Hang the X− hip module on the other side.
Fix it with six M5×10 screws.

steps.title: Upper supports and cover catches
steps.text: The top covers are held by magnets. Their catches are the steel washers under eight M5×6 button-head screws on the top rails.

actions.cap: Fit the two upper supports on the middle rail.
Drop T-nuts into the top channels.
Lay an M5 washer over each T-nut.
Screw the washers down with M5×6 button-head screws.

steps.title: Electronics tray
steps.text: The two printed trays carry the Jetson Orin Nano on one side and the Raspberry Pi 5 with the power distribution board on the other. Fit the Orin on the bench, because its screws go in from underneath, and press the inserts into the power-board bridge there too. The tray goes into the body before the Raspberry Pi, because the Pi covers two of the tray screws.

actions.cap: Set the Raspberry Pi half of the tray on the bench.
Press the two M3 inserts for the joint and the four M2.5 inserts for the Pi.
Set the Orin half next to it.
Join the two halves with two M3×12 screws.
Set the Jetson Orin Nano on its tray.
Fix it from underneath with four M3×8 screws.
Fit the small Orin support.
Set the power-board bridge on the bench.
Press four M2.5 inserts into the bridge.
Drop seven T-nuts into the lower rails.
Lower the tray into the body.
Fix the tray with seven M5×10 countersunk screws.
Set the Raspberry Pi 5 on its side of the tray.
Screw four M2.5×20 standoffs through the Pi into the inserts.
Set the bridge on the standoffs.
Fix it with four M2.5×6 screws. One of them ends up under the power board, so do this before the board goes on.
Set the power distribution board on the bridge.
Fix it with four M2.5×5 screws.

steps.title: Converter shelf
steps.text: The two XL4016 buck converters sit on a printed shelf at the front of the body.

actions.cap: Set the converter shelf on the bench.
Press eight M3 inserts into the shelf.
Place the two converters.
Fix them with eight M3×6 button-head screws.
Drop four T-nuts into the front and middle rails.
Lower the shelf into the front of the body.
Fix it with four M5×10 button-head screws.

steps.title: Camera and front cover
steps.text: The RealSense D435i looks out through the window in the front cover. Its bracket screws to the back of the cover, so build cover, bracket and camera together and fit them as one piece.

actions.cap: Set the front cover on the bench.
Press four M3 inserts into the back of the cover.
Put the camera in the window.
Place the bracket behind the camera.
Fix the camera to the bracket with two M3×6 screws.
Fix the bracket to the cover with four M3×8 screws.
Drop four T-nuts into the front rails.
Offer the cover up to the front of the frame.
Fix it with four M5×10 socket-head screws.

steps.title: Lower frame and IMU
steps.text: Turn the body upside down. The IMU sits on the inside of the lower frame, so fit it while the frame is still on the bench, then put the frame on the bottom rails.

actions.cap: Turn the body over.
Set the two lower-frame halves on the bench, inside face up.
Press two M3 inserts for the IMU.
Stick the IMU on its foam pad.
Fix the IMU with two M3×8 screws.
Drop T-nuts into the bottom channels of the lower rails.
Turn the lower frame over onto the bottom rails.
Fix it with eight M5×12 button-head screws.
Press four M3×4 inserts across the joint between the halves.
Join the halves with four M3×8 countersunk screws.

steps.title: Battery shoe and side covers
steps.text: The printed shoe takes the M18 battery. The two lower side covers close the gaps beside it. In the current model the two front shoe screws sit under the battery rail with nothing open above them, so they cannot be driven once the shoe is in place. Press all four inserts, fit the two rear screws, and leave the front pair out until the shoe gets access holes through the rail.

actions.cap: Press four M3 inserts for the shoe.
Place the battery shoe.
Fix it with the two rear M3×20 button-head screws.
Press the inserts for the side covers and the belly.
Place the two lower side covers.
Fix each cover with three M3×8 countersunk screws.

steps.title: Belly and landing gear
steps.text: Turn the body back over. The landing gear lives in the printed belly: two MG90S servos fold two pairs of legs on D-shafts. Build it in the belly on the bench; the legs stand the belly on the bench while you work.

actions.cap: Turn the body over.
Set the belly shell on the bench.
Put the two servos in their pockets.
Fix each servo with two 2×8 self-tapping screws.
Hold the four legs in place inside the belly.
Slide the 98 mm D-shaft through the side of the belly and the front legs.
Slide the 55 mm D-shaft through the rear legs.
Fit the front lever with its ball stud on the front shaft.
Fit the slotted lever on the rear shaft.
Fit the horn with its ball stud on the front servo.
Fit the crank and its dowel pin on the rear servo; the pin runs in the slotted lever.
Clip the tie rod between the two ball studs.
Press the inserts into the four gear stops.
Hold the stops under the belly.
Fix the stops with eight M3×10 screws from inside.
Push the TPU plugs into the shaft holes.
Push the TPU feet onto the legs.

steps.title: Belly on the body
steps.text: The belly hangs from the lower frame on six M3×10 screws. Reach them from inside through the battery opening at the front.

actions.cap: Set the body down onto the belly.
Fix the belly with six M3×10 countersunk screws from inside.

steps.title: Battery and nose
steps.text: The M18 battery slides into the shoe from the front. The nose closes over it on two pairs of magnets and one M3 screw underneath. In the current model the pocket around that screw is about 15 mm deep for a 30 mm screw, so the screw cannot go in straight with the nose on. Press its insert now and let the magnets hold the nose until the pocket is opened up.

actions.cap: Slide the M18 battery into the shoe until it clicks.
Glue the four Ø6 magnets into the nose and the belly.
Press the insert for the nose screw.
Close the nose. The magnets pull it into place.

chapters.title: Legs
chapters.intro: Each leg is a five-bar linkage: the two hip actuators drive an upper arm each; a shin hangs from the front arm and carries the wheel actuator, and a rear link from the rear arm closes the loop at the wheel axle.

steps.title: Upper arm
steps.text: An arm is two aluminium plates on four M4×27 brass standoffs, with a printed core between them. Build all four the same way; two of them are mirror images.

actions.cap: Lay the inner plate on the bench.
Stand the four brass standoffs on it.
Turn the plate over, holding the standoffs.
Fix them with four M4×8 countersunk screws.
Turn it back.
Fit the printed core between the standoffs.
Lay the thin steel plate and the outer plate on top.
Fix the outer plate with four M4×8 screws.

steps.title: Arms on the hip actuators
steps.text: Each arm bolts to an actuator output flange with six M3×12 countersunk screws, reached through the holes in the outer plate. The hip motors turn freely while unpowered, so you can swing the arms to line up the holes.

actions.cap: Offer the arm up to the front X+ actuator.
Fix it with six M3×12 countersunk screws.
Fit the other three arms the same way.

steps.title: Rear link
steps.text: The rear link is two aluminium plates on brass standoffs around a printed core. Two 608 bearings in the top end ride on the knee shaft; the bottom end clamps the wheel axle.

actions.cap: Lay the inner plate on the bench.
Place the two halves of the printed core.
Press the two 608 bearings into the top end.
Stand the brass standoffs in their holes.
Put the axle spacer in the bottom end.
Lay the outer plate on top.
Screw the outer plate down: M2×6 into the M2 standoffs, M3×6 into the M3 ones.
Turn the link over.
Screw the inner plate down the same way.

steps.title: Shin and wheel actuator
steps.text: The shin has the same plate-and-core construction. The wheel actuator sits across the bottom end on two of the M3 standoffs.

actions.cap: Lay the inner shin plate on the bench.
Place the printed core.
Press the two 608 bearings into the top end.
Fit the wheel actuator, output facing out.
Stand the brass standoffs, two of them through the actuator ears.
Lay the outer plate on top.
Screw the outer plate down.
Turn the shin over.
Screw the inner plate down.
Turn it back, actuator output up.

steps.title: Wheel
steps.text: The rim bolts to the actuator output flange. The axle runs through two 6001 bearings, one in the rim and one in the outer hub, so the rear link can turn freely about the wheel axis.

actions.cap: Set the rim on the bench.
Press six M3 inserts into the rim.
Press a 6001 bearing into the rim hub.
Stretch the tyre over the rim.
Drop the inner axle collar into the output flange.
Set the wheel on the output flange.
Lay the cover disc on the rim.
Fix it with six M3×8 countersunk screws.
Press the second bearing into the outer hub and set hub and shim on the disc.
Clamp hub, disc and rim to the output flange with six M3×30 low-head screws.
Slide the axle through both bearings into the inner collar.

steps.title: Closing the leg
steps.text: The bottom end of the rear link goes over the outer end of the axle. With the link fitted, shin, wheel and link form one lower leg that you offer up to the two arms.

actions.cap: Fit the rear link over the axle end.
Offer the lower leg up to the two arms on the X+ side, knee holes lined up.
Push an Ø8×50 knee shaft through each knee: arm plates and link bearings.
Slide a shaft collar onto each shaft end.
Tighten the collar set screws.

steps.title: The other leg
steps.text: Build the second lower leg as a mirror image and fit it to the X− arms the same way.

actions.cap: Offer up the X− lower leg.
Fit the two knee shafts with their collars.

chapters.title: Covers and lidar
chapters.intro: The covers close the body and the lidar goes on top.

steps.title: Rear covers
steps.text: The back of the body closes with two cover halves that seat on six printed magnet holders on the rear rails.

actions.cap: Fit the six magnet holders on the rear rails.
Fit the two rear cover halves.

steps.title: Top covers and lidar
steps.text: Glue two Ø10 magnets into each top cover. The covers then snap onto the steel washers on the top rails and lift off for access.

actions.cap: Glue two Ø10×3 magnets into each top cover.
Snap the four top covers on.
Set the RPLIDAR A1 in its place on top.
